coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: 1180 Fourth Street
record.summary: A 150-unit affordable apartment building at 1180 Fourth Street in Mission Bay South for low-income families, 50 of them formerly homeless, developed by Mercy Housing California and designed by Mithun (formerly WRT/Solomon E.T.C.), with Kennerly Architecture and Planning as associate design architect. DataSF's Assessor tax roll records the parcel's construction year as 2015, and Mercy Housing held its official opening celebration on May 6, 2015.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL lot geometry -- the outline is Assessor lot 8711501 (6,026 m2, active), so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a surveyed building footprint: it includes any yard, setback or plaza inside the lot and can sit a little off the walls. The lot is condominium-mapped: 4 Assessor lots share this outline (the map lot 8711501 and 3 per-unit lots), so the outline is the building's shared lot, not any one unit. Until 2026-10-12 this record showed the surveyed building footprint (DataSF Building Footprints (mblr SF8711014)); 95% of that outline lies inside the lot and it covered 72% of the lot.

changes.text: 1180 4th Street's May 2015 opening celebration now also cites SFGovTV's video of the event, since the earlier source no longer loads.

The record's summary and map notes named Kennerly Architecture & Planning as lead designer; Mithun's project page shows Mithun (formerly WRT/Solomon E.T.C.) as architect, Kennerly as associate design architect and Full Circle Architects as associate architect. The notes said the building fills a full city block and is 216,000 sq ft; Mithun gives 217,620 sf on 1.4 acres at Fourth and Channel, so the block claim is withdrawn. The completion year is explained (Mithun 2014; DBI permit completed 2015-04-02; Assessor 2015). 'Very-low-income' was removed from the summary because only 'low-income' is sourced, and Mithun was added as a source. The Wikimedia aerial's credit now names only the Commons username Firstcultural, and the NAIP credit names the USDA Farm Production and Conservation Business Center, which the data.gov record names as NAIP's administrator. The May 6, 2015 opening celebration rests on a Mercy Housing page that now returns 404 and is listed among the record's open questions.

open_questions: The Registry's own December 2014 headline says construction was already complete by then, ahead of the May 2015 public opening/dedication; no source found pins down an exact construction-completion (certificate of occupancy) date distinct from the dedication event.
No source found for the total development cost, as of 2026-09-21.

Mercy Housing's May 2015 press page is no longer reachable and could not be checked in September 2026; the May 6 date and the attendees (the Mayor and the District 6 Supervisor) are not re-verified (an Internet Archive snapshot of the page exists but has not been checked). 'Very-low-income' was removed from the summary because no source read states it; Mithun says 'low-income'.
Mithun gives completion 2014 while DBI's permit 201012036075 shows completed 2015-04-02 and the Assessor year built is 2015; the record uses 2015 for the completion year.
